note: Friedrich-manner evening: dead oak on a dark heath hillock, a small Rückenfigur on its shoulder looking out over a hazy marsh with a lagoon catching the glow, far blue hills with a church spire, crescent moon and evening star in a graded dusk sky. Sky body is done and dry; tree and figure painted; the hill is still wet (day 56). I'm wondering most about: (1) whether the figure placement/scale works and whether the composition is too empty on the right, (2) the middle-distance plain (is it convincing as space?), (3) whether the oak reads as Friedrich-like or too generic/regular, (4) whether the sky needs the thin cloud bands I planned.

Please look at the whole and tell me what still weakens it most. I'm unsure about: the twig sprays (do they read as oak or as a repeated 'v' motif?), the dark lower third (too heavy/empty?), and whether the right-hand slope of the hill reads as form.
